definitions.gloss: to contract; to undertake; to take on (a job)
definitions.explanation: To formally agree to take responsibility for a task or project, especially construction, manufacturing, or other professional work, usually under a contract.

examples.japanese: その{工事|こうじ}を{請|う}け{負|お}った。
examples.english: We contracted to do the construction work.

examples.japanese: {大手|おおて}の{建設|けんせつ}{会社|がいしゃ}が{駅|えき}の{改修|かいしゅう}を{請|う}け{負|お}った。
examples.english: A major construction company undertook the renovation of the station.

examples.japanese: {個人|こじん}で{翻訳|ほんやく}の{仕事|しごと}を{請|う}け{負|お}って{生計|せいけい}を{立|た}てている。
examples.english: I make a living by taking on translation work as a freelancer.

notes:
{請|う}け{負|お}う is a transitive godan verb (conjugation: {請|う}け{負|お}わない, {請|う}け{負|お}って, etc.).

ASPECT (ている):
{請|う}け{負|お}っている indicates that someone currently has a contract or is in the process of carrying out contracted work.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- を{請|う}け{負|お}う (to contract for something)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {工事|こうじ}を{請|う}け{負|お}う (to contract for construction)
- {仕事|しごと}を{請|う}け{負|お}う (to take on a job)
- {業務|ぎょうむ}を{請|う}け{負|お}う (to undertake operations)

RELATED WORDS:
The noun form is {請負|うけおい} (contract, contracting). A {請負|うけおい}{業者|ぎょうしゃ} is a contractor.
